strategist.thesis: Teradyne (TER) screens at opportunity 65.0 with an expectations gap of 19.0. Reality 76.0 reflects +57.9% TTM revenue growth, +30.2% operating margin and +41.8% ROIC; pricing 57.0 reflects a fair multiple and neutral price momentum. Primary theme exposure: Semiconductor Capacity Build (trend 64.0). Macro fit for Technology in a Goldilocks regime is 53.0/100.

market_expectation.summary: Priced roughly in line with its own history and peers; the market expects the current trajectory to continue.

llm.thesis: Teradyne is a semiconductor test franchise whose fundamentals have inflected violently — TTM revenue +57.9% (accelerating from +30.3%), operating margin 30.2% (+1,194bps YoY), ROIC 41.8% with incremental ROIC of 122% — on a debt-free balance sheet that is simultaneously shrinking the share count 2.7%. The engine's expectations gap (+19) is directionally right about operating reality running ahead of consensus modeling, but it understates how much the multiple has already moved: EV/Sales of 13.5x sits at the 80th percentile of its own five-year range versus a 6.4x median, and P/FCF of 75.8x prices a durable structural step-up, not a cycle. The genuine debate is therefore not 'cheap vs. expensive' but 'cycle vs. regime': if AI/HBM/advanced-SoC test intensity has permanently raised the ATE revenue-per-wafer content, today's multiple is defensible; if this is a classic capex spike, the incremental ROIC of 122% is a peak-cycle artifact that mean-reverts hard. Price action already reflects that uncertainty — +188% over twelve months but -17.9% over three and -19.9% from the high — meaning the stock is digesting the re-rating rather than extending it. We rate this a constructive but valuation-constrained long: own the operating momentum, but size for multiple compression, and recognize the cleaner risk/reward may sit in Teradyne's consumables and OSAT ecosystem rather than in Teradyne itself.
llm.fundamental_read: Growth, margin and return metrics are all inflecting together, which is the signature of operating leverage on a fixed-cost instrument business: revenue +57.9%, net income +145%, EPS +153%, and operating margin up nearly 1,200bps to 30.2%. Quality is somewhat lower than headline: FCF conversion is only 69.5% and FCF grew +40.6% versus revenue +57.9%, implying working-capital absorption, while a 13.5% tax rate flatters EPS growth relative to pre-tax progress. The balance sheet is pristine — zero debt, net cash of $350m, net debt/EBITDA -0.2x, interest coverage 119x — and capital return is real but modest in yield terms ($501m buybacks, shareholder yield 0.96%). ROE 33.5% and ROA 23.4% confirm this is a high-return, asset-light model, but only 17.9% FCF margin against a 1.3% FCF yield means the cash engine does not currently support the valuation on its own.
llm.technical_read: The primary trend is intact: close 387.7 sits above the 20-day (362), 50-day (367.5) and 200-day (328.7), with a 50>200 uptrend, RSI at a neutral-constructive 55.4 and MACD histogram positive at +4.93. But the 3-month return of -17.9% and a 19.9% drawdown from the 52-week high mark this as a high-volatility consolidation within an uptrend, not a fresh breakout. The 200-day at ~329 is the structural line; a sustained close below ~296 (10% under the 200-day) would confirm the trend has broken and the growth narrative is being repriced.
llm.market_expectation: At 53x earnings (70th percentile of its own history), 40.7x EV/EBITDA and 13.5x EV/Sales versus a 6.4x five-year median, the market is explicitly pricing the current inflection as a multi-year structural regime — AI-driven test intensity, HBM and advanced packaging test content, and a sustained semicap capacity build — rather than a cyclical peak. Embedded expectations include continued high-30s/40s ROIC, no meaningful margin give-back, and revenue growth staying well above the historical ATE cycle average. The 1.3% FCF yield leaves essentially no margin of safety from cash generation; the equity is a pure duration-on-growth instrument. The PEG of 0.34 is the bull's rebuttal, but it is computed off a trailing growth rate that is itself the peak of the acceleration.
what_market_misses: The engine's own framing is internally inconsistent and worth correcting: it claims 'the multiple has not re-rated' while the valuation block shows EV/Sales at the 80th percentile versus a 6.4x historical median. The multiple has more than doubled; the re-rating has largely happened.

Incremental ROIC of 122% is mathematically explosive but is the hallmark of a fixed-cost business at a cyclical utilization peak — it is the metric most likely to mean-revert and the one least likely to be modeled as transient by momentum buyers.

FCF quality is quietly lagging: 69.5% conversion and FCF growth 17 points below revenue growth suggest receivables/inventory build ahead of shipments. In ATE, that build is a leading indicator in both directions.
The 13.5% effective tax rate is doing real work in the +153% EPS figure; normalization would meaningfully reduce reported earnings growth without any operational deterioration.

Theme exposure is the one failing check (trend 58.0, semicap weighted 0.6) — the narrative engine is not confirming acceleration in the underlying theme even as the company's reported numbers accelerate, a divergence that usually resolves toward the theme, not the print.

Two of the twelve checks — estimate revisions and management guidance — are simply not connected. With a 53x multiple, the direction of forward estimates is the single most important variable, and the system is blind to it.

Robotics (Universal Robots/MiR exposure, weighted 0.4) is a real optionality slot that is effectively unpriced in a semicap-dominated narrative; it is also the segment most likely to drag margins if industrial automation demand stays weak.
catalysts: Next quarterly report roughly 90 days after the 2026-07-31 filing: the key tell is whether revenue growth holds above the ~41% thesis-break threshold and whether FCF conversion recovers toward 100%.
Confirmation (or denial) of a third consecutive quarter of operating margin expansion — the +1,194bps YoY move is the core of the bull case and the hardest thing to repeat.
Continued Technology sector rotation (+66, the only sector above +30 alongside Energy at +27) sustaining the multiple.

Evidence that AI infrastructure bottlenecks — GPU supply, HBM, advanced packaging, interconnect — are translating into higher test time per device, which is the mechanism by which the ATE regime shift would become structural.
Recapture of the 52-week high (~484 implied by the -19.9% drawdown) would confirm the consolidation resolved upward.
risks: Valuation is the dominant risk: at 13.5x EV/Sales and 1.3% FCF yield, a deceleration from +57.9% to a still-excellent +30% could compress the multiple toward its 6.4x median and halve the equity without the business ever turning bad.

ATE is historically one of the most cyclical sub-industries in semis; peak incremental ROIC and peak margins have preceded sharp order air-pockets in prior cycles (inference from cycle structure, not from company-specific evidence supplied).
Customer concentration in leading-edge test is typically extreme; a single large customer's capex digestion can reset the revenue base (inference — not confirmed in the evidence provided).

Regime probabilities are near-uniform (Goldilocks 26.6, Reflation 24.6, Contraction 25.4, Stagflation 23.5) — there is no macro tailwind here, only a coin flip, and macro fit for Tech is a mediocre 53/100.
The -17.9% three-month return with the stock still 17.9% above its 200-day means a full mean-reversion to trend is a further ~15% downside before any thesis damage is technically confirmed.
Export-control or China-demand policy shocks are a live tail risk for semicap equipment specifically (speculative — not in evidence).
thesis_break_conditions: TTM revenue growth falls below 41% (currently 57.9%), signaling the acceleration has rolled over.
Operating margin compresses more than 200bps YoY from 30.2%, indicating the operating-leverage story is reversing.
ROIC falls below 31% (currently 41.8%) or incremental ROIC turns negative, confirming peak-cycle utilization.
FCF conversion deteriorates below ~60% for two consecutive quarters, implying the working-capital build is demand-driven rather than shipment-driven.
Price closes more than 10% below the 200-day average (~296) with negative relative strength.
Technology sector rotation score turns below -20 for two consecutive runs (currently +66).
Semiconductor Capacity Build theme trend drops below 45 (currently 64, exposure-weighted narrative already only 58).
EV/Sales pushes above ~16x without a corresponding upgrade to forward growth — at that point the position is a momentum trade, not an expectations-gap trade.
second_order_beneficiaries: Test consumables and interface suppliers — probe cards, sockets, load boards and burn-in boards — whose revenue scales with test insertions and test time rather than with tester unit sales, and which typically carry lower multiples than the tester OEM (e.g., FormFactor, Cohu-type exposure).

OSATs and outsourced test houses (ASE, Amkor, King Yuan-type businesses) that absorb the incremental test volume Teradyne's installed base creates and monetize utilization without carrying the R&D burden.
Advantest and other ATE peers — if the structural test-intensity thesis is right, it is an industry regime, not a share-gain story, and the cheaper peer captures the same tailwind.
HBM and advanced-packaging test specialists: rising stack counts and KGD requirements raise test cost per bit, a bottleneck that pays whoever solves it.

High-speed instrumentation component suppliers — precision power, RF/analog front-ends, high-density connectors and FPGAs inside the testers — which are a constrained input to Teradyne's own throughput.
Automation and material-handling vendors, plus Teradyne's own robotics franchise, if the semicap capacity build extends into fab and back-end labor substitution.

Power and thermal infrastructure providers into AI datacenters — the same bottleneck set the catalyst list names (power availability, liquid cooling, optical interconnect) — which monetize the identical demand driver with different cyclicality.

epistemic_labels.statement: TTM revenue grew 57.9%, accelerating 27.5 points from the prior quarter's 30.3%.
Operating margin is 30.2%, up 1,194bps YoY; ROIC 41.8%; incremental ROIC 122.1%.
Balance sheet carries zero debt, $350m cash, net debt/EBITDA -0.2x, and diluted shares fell 2.7% YoY.
EV/Sales is 13.5x (80th percentile of the 5y range) versus a 5y median of 6.4x; P/E 52.7x; FCF yield 1.3%.
The stock is +187.9% over 12 months, -17.9% over 3 months, and 19.9% below its 52-week high while sitting 17.9% above its 200-day average.
FCF conversion of 69.5% and FCF growth of 40.6% versus revenue growth of 57.9% imply working-capital absorption.
The market expects the current growth trajectory to persist as a structural regime rather than a cyclical peak.
The engine's claim that 'the multiple has not re-rated' is contradicted by its own 80th-percentile EV/Sales reading.
122% incremental ROIC is characteristic of a fixed-cost business at peak utilization and is the metric most likely to mean-revert.
A 13.5% effective tax rate materially flatters the +153% EPS growth figure relative to underlying pre-tax progress.
Test consumables suppliers and OSATs capture the same test-intensity tailwind at lower multiples than the tester OEM.
Customer concentration in leading-edge ATE is extreme enough that one customer's capex digestion could reset the revenue base.
AI-driven test-time-per-device expansion (HBM stacks, advanced packaging, KGD) has permanently raised ATE content per wafer, justifying a multiple above the historical median.
Export-control or China-demand policy action is a live tail risk for semicap equipment.
The robotics segment represents unpriced optionality but could also drag consolidated margins if industrial automation demand stays soft.
